title: The Quantification of Injectability by Mechanical Testing
protocol: Prepare the sample and load it into the syringe.
To simulate a pre-loaded syringe, prepare the sample in advance.
Load the prepared sample into the syringe.
Attach the needle to the loaded syringe.
Store the syringe as required until testing.
For hydrogels and materials that do not change with time, prepare the sample in advance for stability.
Dissolve 2 g of alginic acid sodium salt in 100 mL of deionized water by stirring at room temperature.
Aspirate the solution into 5 mL syringes.
Store the prepared alginate solutions for 24 h at room temperature.
To simulate an injection formulated directly prior to application, prepare the sample as it would be made in the clinic.
Manually mix 4 g of calcium sulfate hemihydrate with 5 mL of deionized water using a spatula for 1 min.
Remove the plunger from the syringe and load the cement into the syringe barrel using the spatula.
Begin mechanical testing after 4 min for calcium sulfate cement.
Attach flat platens to the mechanical tester for compression testing.
Equip the mechanical tester with a load cell with a maximum load of 200 N.
Separate the plates to allow sufficient space for the needle, syringe, and plunger (around 30 cm).
Open the test wizard and set the test type to uniaxial compression.
Set the pre-load value to 0.5 N.
Set the speed to pre-load to 5 mm/min.
Select an appropriate test speed of 1 mm/s for a standard 5 mL syringe.
Set an upper force limit at which to stop the test, e.g., 200 N.
Attach two sets of clamps to two stands with grips large enough to securely hold the chosen syringe.
Place the grips between the crosshead and baseplate, ensuring there is enough space below for the syringe and needle.
Line up the centers of the two grips with the center of the crosshead.
Align the clamp grips with each other and the center of the crosshead.
Secure the clamps firmly so that there is no movement when downward force is applied.
Place a dish onto the bottom plate to collect extruded material.
Insert the syringe into the clamp grips and close them.
Lower the top plate to a position just above the plunger using manual movement buttons.
Zero the measured force by clicking ‘Zero Force’.
Run the testing protocol by pressing ‘Run’.
Raise the plates to a sufficient height, using the manual movement buttons, so that the syringe can be removed.
Repeat step 4 for each sample.
Discard the syringe and extruded sample if no further analysis is required.
Save data from each trial in a format that can generate a table of force and displacement values (.txt, .xls, .xlsx).
Plot results from each trial with displacement on the x-axis and force on the y-axis.
Read the maximum force from the graphs if it exists.
Determine the plateau force from the graphs.
